title: The Last Vector Again
premise: Orsen Hartwell, a disgraced insurance investigator hiding among cargo haulers in contested orbits, discovers the nine-second gravity flicker was a handshake test from an ancient alien lattice buried beneath Ceres—one that has chosen him, through his dead sister's stolen neural imprint, as its translator. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence and two rival fleets edge toward war over who controls the signal, Orsen must sustain a fabricated lie: that he alone can speak for the lattice. In the end, he sacrifices his anonymity and his chance at a quiet life with engineer Sefa Okonkwo, broadcasting the truth of both fleets' shared guilt into the lattice so it spares humanity—vanishing into the deep dark with the machine, but leaving behind a found family that carries his voice forward.
about_author: Jude Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people who keep systems running while history happens overhead.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. During a routine insurance audit aboard the freighter Kestrel's Debt, gravity fails system-wide for exactly nine seconds; Orsen alone notices his implant recorded a patterned pulse during the blackout. The beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: The Claim Nobody Filed
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Investigating damage claims, he finds every affected ship received the same pulse signature, and one claimant—a Ceres mining widow—died the same night. Emotional beat: guilt resurfaces as he recognizes his sister's neural watermark inside the pulse.

chapters.title: Sefa's Hands
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Okonkwo, Kestrel's engineer. She repairs the ship's gravitic dampeners and realizes they didn't fail—they answered something. She covers for Orsen without knowing why, and the chapter lands on tentative trust becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Earth's last transmission loop enters its final cycle; the Concord fleet and the Meridian Compact both converge on Ceres, each believing the other triggered the flicker. Orsen must decide whether to stay hidden or use what he knows. Beat: duty versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: What Mira Left Running
chapters.summary: POV Orsen, flashback-woven. He traces his sister Mira's old research station on Ceres and finds her consciousness partially resident in the lattice—an echo that calls him by a childhood name. Beat: grief transformed into terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Orsen fabricates evidence that he's the lattice's authorized envoy, buying a ceasefire window between fleets. Sefa catches the forgery—and chooses to help him maintain it. Beat: complicity as intimacy; love choosing the lie.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Aphelion
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A Concord intelligence officer, Vess Arda, dismantles his story piece by piece, offering him amnesty for betrayal. Orsen refuses, and the lattice itself intervenes, flickering gravity around Vess's ship. Beat: the mask becomes real; fear hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown Loop
chapters.summary: POV alternating Orsen/Sefa. With hours left in Earth's transmission loop, both fleets arm for a strike on Ceres, and the lattice demands a translator's oath that would erase Mira's echo permanently. Beat: everything converges; no clean choices remain.

chapters.title: The Last Vector
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. At the lattice's heart, Orsen broadcasts not commands but testimony—both fleets' histories of harm and rescue woven together—convincing the machine humanity is worth its attention. He says goodbye to Mira and to Sefa across an open channel. Climax: sacrifice against duty, love spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Carry the Voice
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, months later. Gravity holds steady, the fleets sign an uneasy accord brokered by Orsen's transmitted record, and Sefa leads the crew that keeps his broadcast looping toward the stars. Final beat: grief braided with hope; found family as inheritance.
